articles.excerpt: Rajkumar Periasamy's Tamil spy thriller O.M: Operation Mole reached Rs 104.58 crore worldwide in six days, even as daily collections fell from an Rs 18.1 crore opening day.
articles.nri_angle: A Tamil tentpole crossing Rs 100 crore worldwide, with Rs 26.75 crore from overseas markets, reflects the diaspora audience's weight in Kollywood's economics.

articles.title: Centre Asks Netflix to Keep Pakistani Series 'Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo' Out of India
articles.excerpt: The Information and Broadcasting Ministry has told Netflix to adhere to its May 2025 advisory and honour its June 2025 commitment, after complaints over the Fawad Khan and Mahira Khan series due to premiere globally on December 4.
articles.image_caption: Netflix logos displayed at a company event.
articles.nri_angle: The series premieres globally on December 4, so diaspora viewers outside India can watch it even as its availability on Netflix India is blocked.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

dates.event: Netflix informed the ministry it had made no Pakistani content available to Indian subscribers.

items.text: The May 8, 2025 advisory was issued after the April 22, 2025 Pahalgam terror attack.
In the attack, 26 people were killed.

articles.title: Ramayana Closes Day 20 at ₹972.95 Crore Net, ₹27 Crore From ₹1,000 Crore Club
articles.excerpt: The Nitesh Tiwari epic earned ₹17.50 crore on its third Tuesday and stands at ₹1,735.15 crore worldwide, set to become only the fourth Indian film to collect ₹1,000 crore net in India.
articles.image_caption: Promotional art for Ramayana: Part 1 showing Ranbir Kapoor as Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita and Ravi Dubey as Lakshman. The film closed Day 20 at ₹972.95 crore net in India, according to Sacnilk.
articles.nri_angle: Overseas audiences have contributed ₹573 crore of Ramayana's worldwide gross, making diaspora theatres central to its record run.

articles.title: Film Workers' Body Asks PM Modi to Block Fawad Khan's Pakistani Netflix Series in India
articles.excerpt: The All India Cine Workers Association wants Jo Bachay Hain Sang Samait Lo kept off Netflix India ahead of its December 4 global premiere, and a permanent law against Pakistani content on Indian platforms.
articles.image_caption: Pakistani actor Fawad Khan. A film workers' body has asked Prime Minister Narendra Modi to block Khan's Pakistani Netflix series from release in India.
articles.nri_angle: The demand targets Netflix India only; the series' December 4 global premiere is unaffected, so diaspora viewers in the US and elsewhere will be able to watch it on Netflix where they live.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Ramayana Nears ₹1,700 Crore Worldwide, Passes Dhurandhar 2 in the US
articles.excerpt: Day 18 added ₹35.60 crore net in India as the worldwide gross hit ₹1,693.50 crore — and its $28.4 million US total is now the highest ever for an Indian film.
articles.image_caption: Ranbir Kapoor as Rama and Sai Pallavi as Sita in Ramayana. The film reached Rs 1,693.50 crore worldwide gross in 18 days and set a new all-time US record for an Indian film at $28.4 million.
articles.nri_angle: The film's $28.4 million US total is a new all-time benchmark for an Indian film in America, with overseas markets supplying a third of its global gross.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A. R. Rahman Spent Three Years on 'Ramayana' Music, Turned Down 10–12 Films
articles.excerpt: At IFFI in Panaji, the composer said he set aside almost everything else for Nitesh Tiwari's two-part epic, co-composing with Hans Zimmer — some pieces went through 12–13 versions.
articles.image_caption: A. R. Rahman with the Banaras team at a press conference during the International Film Festival of India in Goa.
articles.nri_angle: Rahman and Hans Zimmer's three-year score is the musical backbone of the Diwali epic diaspora audiences are watching in theatres now.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Ramayana: Part 1 Collects ₹64.10 Crore in Kerala in 17 Days
articles.excerpt: Trade tracker AB George's figures show the Nitesh Tiwari epic rebounding in its third Kerala weekend, while Pinkvilla puts its all-India nett at ₹850.50 crore and its dubbed versions past a ₹200 crore first.
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora audiences, the Kerala numbers underline how the film's dubbed versions — not just the Hindi original — are driving one of the biggest Indian theatrical runs of the year.
